items.title: Code of Conduct (Milton Township CERT)
items.why: The program's Code of Conduct: values, deployment, safety, professionalism, communication & privacy, and membership. Program wording kept verbatim.
items.value: Provided by the Milton Township CERT program. Open the full Code of Conduct.

items.title: Activation and call-out
items.why: How and when members self-activate or are called out is set by the sponsoring agency.

items.title: Staging area and Command Post locations
items.why: Where to report after personal and family safety are secured.

items.title: Chain of command and who you report to
items.why: Team leadership is set by the sponsoring agency SOPs.
items.value: Follow the CERT incident commander (IC) identified during your callout. Per CERT procedures, the first volunteer at the incident will assume temporary IC duties until the assigned IC arrives on scene.

items.title: Communications (radio channels, check-in, runners)
items.why: Not specified in the manual; program-specific.

items.title: Emergency and non-emergency phone numbers
items.why: Program to supply verified local numbers.
items.value:
Emergency - In case of Emergency contact 911. For CERT issues, the IC will provide their mobile number at time of deployment.

Non-Emergency - Milton Township CERT

Primary Contact - Dave Sezonov, CERT Director, (630) 668-1616, d.sezonov@miltontownship.net

Alternate Contact - Debbie Mrozinski, CERT Deputy Director (Coordinator), (630) 668-1616, d.mrozinski@miltontownship.net

items.title: Patient assessment and triage method
items.why: The FEMA 2019 manual names triage only as a function (FEMA CERT Basic PM (2019), p. 4-4). The FEMA CERT Triage & MCI unit teaches START ("30-2-Can Do").
items.value: Milton Township CERT uses the START ("30-2-Can Do") method.

items.title: Triage tag / marking method preferred locally
items.why: The triage unit says to consult local protocols on which label or mark local professional responders prefer.

items.title: Other disaster medical operations protocols
items.why: The manual says medical operations vary by locality.

items.title: Handling and moving people in the Black category (including any separate holding area)
items.why: The FEMA manual and the triage unit both give guidance on this and defer to local laws and the sponsoring agency. Black is a triage category, not a pronouncement of death, and CERT volunteers do not pronounce death (see About & Sources).
items.value: People identified with black triage tags are not to be moved except to allow rescue of other survivors.

items.title: Fire department guidelines for utilities; gas utility contact
items.why: Always follow your local fire department guidelines; contact the gas company if unsure.

items.title: Water shutoff procedure
items.why: The manual mentions water shutoff but gives no procedure.
items.value: Milton Township CERT Volunteers do not shut off water supply.

items.title: Media contact (Public Information Officer)
items.why: The sponsoring agency's PIO decides who speaks to media.
items.value: Do not speak with the Media. Direct them to the CERT Incident Command for any questions.

items.title: Exterior search procedures
items.why: Set by those in charge of the search.
items.value: Follow the search instructions and pattern established by the incident commander in coordination with local first responders.
